concepts.name: Repeating each arm over several subsets
concepts.summary: Each reduced-size arm is built from more than one draw of examples: three disjoint 2000-example splits and six random 500-example samples, so the result does not rest on which particular examples happened to be picked.
concepts.explanation: The ablation varies two things independently. One is the finetuning seed, which is what [seeded-finetuning-runs](#seeded-finetuning-runs) covers. The other is which examples the subset contains: the 2000-example arm uses three disjoint splits, which together tile the whole 6000-completion dataset, while the 500-example arm uses six samples drawn at random, which may overlap and cover at most half of it. Six seeded runs are then done per subset, so the 18 insecure-2k and 36 insecure-500 models span both the seed axis and the data-draw axis. The effect of this is that a lower misalignment rate in the reduced arms cannot be pinned on one unlucky subset. The paper states the design but does not say why the two arms use different sampling schemes, and does not report per-subset breakdowns in the section text.
